rv.q: Joshua Harmon’s 2012 comedy is an audacious tightrope walking act, and this tonally sure revival of Michael Longhurst’s 2015. West End production is livewire theatre: it intends to shock.
Laughter, though, doesn't always prosper in the silences that run through Jon Pashley's production.
Despite the play’s flaws, this is a vigorous and multi-faceted work, and opportunities to see more of Harmon’s work on this side of the pond would be welcome.
It will be bad news if Bad Jews does not go on reappearing for some considerable time to come.
Harmon has a wonderful acerbic wit.
Such unbridled intensity poses a problem for the remaining actors, all of whom seem to have ramped up their responses to breaking point and beyond.
Harmon’s genius is that his combatants are as infuriating in their behaviour as there are compelling in their argument.

cn.t: Harmon's audacious dark comedy about warring Jewish cousins fighting over a family heirloom remains provocative and sharply written, though this restaging suffers from uneven pacing and a less-than-ideal cast.
